rows.selection_reason: No completed experiments exist, so the main uncertainty is the performance floor and which design axes are worth exploring. config_001 is the simplest RNA-only, single-profile PCA baseline, giving a low-cost reference for validation accuracy and F1. It will help calibrate later comparisons of multiprofile aggregation, alternative RNA encoders, and image/multimodal fusion while avoiding simultaneous changes to many design choices.

The only completed experiment is RNA-only PCA single-profile, with validation accuracy 0.4849 and F1 0.4639, so there is no evidence yet about whether image features are informative or whether multimodal fusion can help. config_010 tests a simple image-only ResNet50 single-profile baseline, reducing uncertainty about the importance of the image modality with minimal added complexity and a budget-friendly encoder. This establishes the image reference needed before evaluating fusion, multiprofile aggregation, or more complex RNA encoders.

RNA-only PCA singleprofile is much stronger than image-only ResNet singleprofile in both accuracy and F1, so the RNA branch is the most promising direction, but only one RNA encoder has been tested. config_004 changes only the RNA encoder to scvi_n200 while keeping rna_only and singleprofile, isolating whether a learned RNA representation improves over PCA before adding multiprofile aggregation or multimodal fusion. This is the most efficient next experiment because it reduces uncertainty about representation with a minimal change, and the result will guide whether later multiprofile or multimodal tests should use PCA or a learned encoder.

RNA-only scvi_n200 is currently the strongest configuration (accuracy 0.520, F1 0.498), clearly better than RNA-only PCA and much better than image-only ResNet50. The main uncertainty is whether the best RNA encoder can be improved by using multiple profiles with a simple aggregation. config_005 tests this logical extension by keeping scvi_n200 and adding multiprofile with avgpool, avoiding an unnecessary jump to transformer aggregation or multimodal fusion. It is the most informative next step because it directly evaluates whether profile aggregation helps the best known representation before testing more complex designs.

The strongest result so far is config_005 (RNA-only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool), with validation accuracy 0.650 and F1 0.628, showing that multiprofile aggregation is highly beneficial. The main remaining uncertainty in this promising direction is whether a learned transformer aggregation can improve over simple average pooling. config_006 tests this by changing only the aggregation method while keeping the best-known RNA encoder and profile setting fixed. This is the best next use of budget because it directly extends the current best configuration, isolates the effect of aggregation, and will inform whether transformer aggregation should be used in later multimodal experiments.

The strongest evidence is that scvi-based RNA multiprofile models (~0.65 acc) substantially outperform singleprofile RNA models (~0.48-0.52 acc), but it is unclear whether the gain comes from multiprofile aggregation itself or from the scvi representation. config_002 tests pca_n2000 with multiprofile avgpool, directly comparing to config_001 while keeping the RNA encoder fixed. This isolates the effect of profile setting and aggregation, clarifies whether multiprofile helps even with a simpler encoder, and avoids adding image/fusion complexity before the RNA design space is better understood.

RNA-only multiprofile models are the strongest evidence so far, with scvi_n200 + transformer slightly ahead of scvi_n200 + avgpool, while pca_n2000 + avgpool is clearly lower. The missing pca_n2000 + transformer point would clarify whether the small transformer advantage is general or specific to scvi_n200, completing a clean comparison of RNA encoder and aggregation. This is a focused, single-factor extension of the strongest direction and is more informative now than moving to multimodal fusion, since image-only ResNet50 is weak and multimodal tests would change multiple design choices at once.

The strongest evidence so far is that RNA multiprofile with scvi_n200 and transformer aggregation is the best setting, outperforming PCA and single-profile baselines. The key remaining uncertainty is whether the untested scgpt RNA encoder can improve on scvi_n200 under this same strong profile/aggregation setting. config_009 changes only the RNA encoder relative to the current best, isolating representation quality. This is a clean exploitation of the most promising direction and is more informative than jumping to multimodal fusion, which would change several factors at once.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile RNA with scvi_n200 and avgpool is near-best, while the only image experiment, single-profile ResNet50, was weak. config_011 tests whether the image modality becomes informative under the same multiprofile/avgpool treatment, keeping ResNet50 fixed so the result mainly reflects profile/aggregation and modality rather than a new image encoder or fusion. avgpool is preferred because it is the more robust multiprofile aggregation in the RNA evidence. If this improves, multimodal ResNet50 extensions become justified; if not, it argues against further ResNet50-based multimodal investment.

The strongest evidence so far is RNA-only multiprofile with scvi_n200 and transformer aggregation, reaching 0.653 accuracy and 0.628 F1, clearly ahead of PCA and scGPT settings. Image-only ResNet50 is weak, especially single-profile, so the key uncertainty is whether image features can add complementary value to the strong RNA representation. config_033 keeps the best RNA design fixed and adds ResNet50 image features with weighted fusion, directly testing whether multimodal fusion improves over the RNA-only baseline while allowing the weak image modality to be downweighted. It is the best next use of budget because it is a minimal, logical extension of the current best direction, avoids confounding with the untested ViT image encoder, and will clarify whether further multimodal or image-encoder exploration is worthwhile.
